answer: Paragraph 10 and footnote 1 support continuing ultimate responsibility despite outsourcing. They do not supply a complete test for fulfillment. A justified conclusion would require an applicable standard and evidence distinguishing retained authority, actual supervision, and operational and ownership-record outcomes. Contractual allocation, a supervision entry, or a completed reconciliation alone does not establish fulfillment; nor does establishing that the requirement applies.

claims.inference: Text: outsourcing does not displace the Product Provider’s ultimate responsibility. Deduction: delegation of tasks cannot by itself establish either release from responsibility or fulfillment.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained edition to the product, entity, activity and assessment period, including relevant conditions and modifications.
Evidence that the assessed entity is the relevant Product Provider.
claims.proposition: Responsibility remains with the Product Provider despite outsourcing.
claims.status: Supported by the retained text; application conditional

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.
the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds.

claims.inference: Proposed evidential judgment: contracts and governance arrangements could show that the provider retains decision-making, information access, escalation and intervention powers. Whether those powers suffice requires a justified standard; paragraph 10 does not enumerate them as a safe harbour. Register maintenance by another permitted actor does not resolve the provider’s separate ultimate responsibility.
missing_premises: Actual contracts, delegations, governance arrangements and enforceable powers.
An applicable standard explaining which retained powers establish responsibility.
For UT 6.8, applicability and the actual scheme, trustee or appointed-person role.
claims.proposition: Allocation of authority is relevant evidence of retained responsibility, but formal allocation alone does not establish fulfillment.
claims.status: Proposed assessment approach, not an express sufficiency test

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible
The scheme, or in the case of a unit trust, the trustee or the person so appointed by the trustee must maintain a register of holders.

claims.inference: Deduction: evidence that supervision occurred answers a different question from whether it was adequate. Proposed assessment evidence includes review scope, competent personnel, findings, escalation, corrective action and coverage over time. UT 6.11C supplies an express supervision standard only for its specified valuation context; transferring it to all tokenisation supervision needs a separate warrant.
missing_premises: A legally applicable supervision standard, including the required scope and cadence.
Evidence of the substance, competence, continuity and effectiveness of supervision.
If relying on UT 6.11C, management-company status and outsourced valuation within its scope.
claims.proposition: Actual supervisory conduct must be assessed separately from authority and from a mere record of a supervision event.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.
The valuation activities of such third party should be subject to ongoing supervision and periodic review by the management company.

claims.inference: Text: operational soundness and ownership records are substantive subjects of responsibility; paragraph 11 separately requires proper records and compatibility. Deduction: a reconciliation’s completion does not establish that records accurately reflect legally valid interests or that discrepancies were resolved. Proposed evidence includes reconciliation results, exceptions and corrections, legally supported ownership mappings, and operational testing over the relevant period. These are evidential proposals, not a source-prescribed exhaustive checklist or guarantee of compliance.
missing_premises: Applicable standards for operational soundness, proper records and compatibility.
Actual ownership rights, settlement arrangements, record coverage and accuracy.
Reconciliation scope, results, unresolved discrepancies and remediation.
Operational incidents, testing and controls across the assessment period.
claims.proposition: Operational and record-keeping outcomes require their own assessment; an activity log or favourable isolated outcome cannot establish overall fulfillment.

support.quote: Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.
For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

whether the ownership interest of the underlying assets of the Tokenised Securities are legally valid under the applicable governing laws, whether there are regular reconciliations between the records for the extrinsic rights and the records for the distributed ledger tokens, or whether any encumbrance affects the extrinsic rights.

rival_readings: Allocation-focused reading: paragraph 10 principally fixes ultimate accountability notwithstanding delegation; detailed performance requirements arise from accompanying provisions.
Conduct-focused reading: remaining responsible for management entails substantive oversight, but the quoted provisions do not specify a complete supervision test.
Outcome-focused reading: operational soundness and proper ownership records are substantive requirements; the text does not settle whether every adverse outcome necessarily establishes failure.
Combined reading: assess allocation, conduct and outcomes together. This is a defensible assessment proposal, but the retained text does not establish that any specified combination is sufficient.
unresolved: The applicable legal or regulatory standard for concluding fulfillment, including the force of “should” and the relationship between responsibility, reasonable conduct and outcomes.
Actual authority, supervision and operational evidence for the relevant entity and period.
Whether defects establish breach, what remediation achieves, and whether any conclusion can extend beyond the assessed period.
Formal rule applicability, graph acceptance and successful serialization do not establish source-to-rule validity or legal fulfillment.
